An interactive button component with multiple visual variants, sizes, and states.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Button } from './design-system/Button';

<Button onPress={() => console.log('Pressed')}>Click me</Button>
```

### Variants

```tsx
<Button variant="primary" onPress={handlePress}>Primary</Button>
<Button variant="secondary" onPress={handlePress}>Secondary</Button>
<Button variant="tertiary" onPress={handlePress}>Tertiary</Button>
<Button variant="link" onPress={handlePress}>Link</Button>
```

### Disabled

```tsx
<Button disabled onPress={handlePress}>Unavailable</Button>
```

### Small size

```tsx
<Button size="sm" onPress={handlePress}>Compact</Button>
```

### Full width

```tsx
<Button isFullWidth onPress={handlePress}>Full width</Button>
```

### With icons

```tsx
<Button leftIcon={<MyIcon />} onPress={handlePress}>
  Add item
</Button>
```

### Icon-only

Requires `accessibilityLabel` — no visible text, so the screen reader label must be explicit:

```tsx
<Button
  leftIcon={<CloseIcon />}
  accessibilityLabel="Close"
  onPress={handlePress}
/>
```

## Accessibility

### Built-in

- Has `button` accessibility role
- Exposes `disabled` state to assistive technologies
- Uses `children` string as the accessibility label automatically
- Dev warnings logged for icon-only buttons missing `accessibilityLabel`

### Usage

- Always provide `accessibilityLabel` for icon-only buttons
- Add `accessibilityHint` to describe the action result when the label alone is insufficient

## Platform behaviour

### Pressed state

While pressed, button opacity reduces to `0.7` (secondary/tertiary/link) or background shifts to `colorInteractiveActive` (primary). Disabled buttons have `0.4` opacity and do not respond to press.

## API compatibility with dds-react-native

The standalone `Button` implements the core API subset. The dds-react-native `Button` adds:

| Feature | Standalone | dds-react-native |
|---------|-----------|-----------------|
| `variant` primary/secondary/tertiary/link | ✅ | ✅ |
| `disabled` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `isFullWidth` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `leftIcon` / `rightIcon` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `accessibilityLabel` / `accessibilityHint` | ✅ | ✅ |
| `isLoading` (spinner) | ❌ | ✅ |
| `isSelected` | ❌ | ✅ |
| `enableHaptics` | ❌ | ✅ |
| `transparent` variant | ❌ | ✅ |
| `componentTokens` | ❌ | ✅ |

A self-contained React Native design system that mirrors the public API of dds-react-native components with zero external dependencies.

## Overview

The standalone design system lives entirely in `src/design-system/`. It has **zero `@ddsrn/*` dependencies** — everything needed is either a React Native primitive or inlined code.

## Why standalone?

This design system exists to demonstrate that the **migration path** (bare RN -> Expo -> Web) is purely a tooling concern, not a component concern. The same component API works on all three targets without modification.

## API compatibility with dds-react-native

All components use the same prop names as their `@ddsrn/components` counterparts. Migrating back to the real library is a one-line import change per file:

```tsx
// Standalone
import { Heading } from './design-system/Heading';

// Real library
import { Heading } from '@ddsrn/components/Heading';
```

The prop API is identical.

## Components

| Component | File | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| [ThemeProvider & useTheme](/design-system/theme) | `theme/ThemeProvider.tsx` | Context provider + hook |
| [Heading](/design-system/heading) | `Heading.tsx` | Semantic heading with level and visual size |
| [BodyText](/design-system/body-text) | `BodyText.tsx` | Body copy with size and content style |
| [Button](/design-system/button) | `Button.tsx` | Interactive button with 4 variants |
| [TopBar](/design-system/top-bar) | `TopBar.tsx` | Navigation bar with title and slots |

## Tokens

All design values are defined in `src/design-system/theme/tokens.ts`:

- **Colours** — Tesco light brand palette (typography, interaction, border, background)
- **Typography** — font sizes (`size12` through `size64`), line heights, font weights
- **Spacing** — `none`, `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, `xxl`
- **Border radius** — `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `pill`

## Usage

```tsx
import { Button } from './design-system/Button';

// Primary (default)

<Button disabled>Unavailable</Button>

// Small
```

Navigation bar with title and left/right slots. Platform-aware title alignment. API-compatible with @ddsrn/components/TopBar.

## Usage

```tsx
import { TopBar } from './design-system/TopBar';

// Simple title
<TopBar title="My Screen" />

// With left/right slots
<TopBar
  title="Settings"
  left={<BackButton />}
  right={<SaveButton />}
/>

// No border
<TopBar title="Fullscreen" hasBorder={false} />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `title` | `string` | — | Centre title text |
| `left` | `ReactNode` | — | Left slot — typically a back button |
| `right` | `ReactNode` | — | Right slot — typically an action button |
| `hasBorder` | `boolean` | `true` | Show 1px bottom border (`StyleSheet.hairlineWidth`) |
| `style` | `ViewStyle` | — | Container style overrides |

## Platform behaviour

| Platform | Title alignment | Min height |
|----------|----------------|------------|
| iOS | Centred | 44px |
| Android | Left-aligned | 56px |
| Web | Centred | 44px |

This matches the `dds-react-native` TopBar behaviour — iOS follows Apple HIG, Android follows Material Design.

## Accessibility

- Container: `accessibilityRole="none"` (not a landmark)
- Title text: `accessibilityRole="header"` (announced by screen readers as a heading)

A complete guide to migrating a React Native app with a standalone design system to Expo, Expo Web, and beyond.

## What this guide covers

This guide documents the migration path of the **DDS React Native Hello World** application through 5 phases — from a bare React Native baseline to a fully web-capable Expo app with automated screenshots and a documentation site.

The application was built with a **standalone design system** (`src/design-system/`) that mirrors the public API of `dds-react-native` components — with no external `@ddsrn/*` package dependencies. This makes the migration portable and demonstrable in isolation.

## Migration path

| Phase | What changes | Screen code changes |
|-------|-------------|-------------------|
| [Phase 1 — Bare React Native](/migration/phase-1-bare-rn) | Baseline: bare RN + standalone design system | — |
| [Phase 2 — Expo SDK](/migration/phase-2-expo) | 5 config files only | None |
| [Phase 3 — Expo Web](/migration/phase-3-expo-web) | 3 web deps added | None |
| [Phase 4 — Screenshots](/migration/phase-4-screenshots) | Playwright script added | None |
| [Phase 5 — Astro Docs](/migration/phase-5-astro-docs) | This docs site | None |

## Key principle

> `git diff phase-1/bare-rn phase-3/expo-web -- src/` outputs **0 lines**.

The screen component and the entire design system are never touched across the migration. Only build tooling and configuration changes.

Enabling browser rendering via react-native-web. The app runs identically in iOS, Android, and a browser — with no screen code changes.

## Goal

Enable the Hello World screen to run **in a browser** via `react-native-web`, with no changes to `src/`.

## Dependencies added

```bash
npx expo install react-dom react-native-web @expo/metro-runtime
```

| Package | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `react-dom` | React's browser renderer |
| `react-native-web` | Maps RN primitives (`View`, `Text`, `Pressable`) to DOM elements |
| `@expo/metro-runtime` | Expo's Metro runtime shim for web |

## Version alignment

Both `react` and `react-dom` must be the exact same version. Expo 53 expects `19.0.0`:

```json
"react":     "19.0.0",
"react-dom": "19.0.0"
```

## `app.json` — web bundler

```json
{
  "expo": {
    "web": { "bundler": "metro" }
  }
}
```

Metro is used as the web bundler (not webpack), which is the Expo SDK 53 default.

## Running on web

```bash
expo start --web --port 4477
# Opens http://localhost:4477 in the browser
```

## DDS component web compatibility

All 5 standalone design-system components are web-compatible out of the box:

| Component | Web status | Reason |
|-----------|-----------|--------|
| `ThemeProvider` | Works | Pure React context |
| `useTheme` | Works | Pure React hook |
| `Heading` | Works | `Text` -> `<span>` via react-native-web |
| `BodyText` | Works | `Text` -> `<span>` |
| `Button` | Works | `Pressable` -> `<div>` with event handlers |
| `TopBar` | Works | `View` -> `<div>` |

No SVG, no reanimated, no gesture-handler — the standalone design system has zero native-only deps.

Building this documentation site using Astro and Starlight, mirroring the dds-react-native docs framework independently.

## Goal

Build a local Astro + Starlight docs site inside `docs/` that:

- Documents all 5 migration phases with code diffs
- Embeds the screenshots captured in Phase 4
- Mirrors the framework pattern of `dds-react-native/apps/docs/` without copying files

## Framework

| Tool | Version | Role |
|------|---------|------|
| [Astro](https://astro.build) | 7.3.2 | Static site generator |
| [@astrojs/starlight](https://starlight.astro.build) | 0.42.0 | Docs theme with sidebar, search, dark mode |

## Structure

```
docs/
├── package.json            # Astro + Starlight dependencies
├── astro.config.mjs        # Starlight sidebar config
├── tsconfig.json           # Extends astro/tsconfigs/strict
└── src/
    ├── content.config.ts   # Starlight docsLoader + docsSchema
    ├── assets/
    │   └── screenshots/    # PNGs from Phase 4 (copied in Phase 5)
    └── content/
        └── docs/
            ├── migration/  # Migration phase guides
```

```bash
npm install

npm run build   # outputs to dist/

```

API reference for the standalone Button component. Props, variants, accessibility state, and usage notes.

:::note
See [Button](/components/button/) for usage guidance, accessibility advice, and platform behaviour.
:::

An interactive button built from React Native `Pressable`. All styling derived from theme tokens — no hardcoded colours.

```tsx
import { Button } from './design-system/Button';
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "tertiary" \| "link"` | `"primary"` | Visual style variant |
| `size` | `"md" \| "sm"` | `"md"` | Button size — affects height, padding and font size |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables interaction, applies 0.4 opacity |
| `isFullWidth` | `boolean` | `false` | Stretches button to fill container width (`alignSelf: "stretch"`) |
| `onPress` | `(event: GestureResponderEvent) => void` | — | Press handler |
| `onPressIn` | `(event: GestureResponderEvent) => void` | — | Called when press begins |
| `onPressOut` | `(event: GestureResponderEvent) => void` | — | Called when press ends |
| `leftIcon` | `ReactNode` | — | Icon displayed before the label |
| `rightIcon` | `ReactNode` | — | Icon displayed after the label |
| `children` | `string \| ReactNode` | — | Button label |
| `style` | `StyleProp<ViewStyle>` | — | Additional container styles |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `string` | Auto from `children` | Screen reader label. Required for icon-only buttons |
| `accessibilityHint` | `string` | — | Additional hint for screen readers |

## Variants

| Variant | Background | Text | Border |
|---------|-----------|------|--------|
| `primary` | `colorInteractiveDefault` | `colorInteractiveInverse` | None |
| `secondary` | `colorInteractiveInverse` | `colorInteractiveDefault` | 1px `colorInteractiveDefault` |
| `tertiary` | Transparent | `colorInteractiveDefault` | None |
| `link` | Transparent | `colorInteractiveDefault` | None + underline |

Pressed state for `primary` shifts background to `colorInteractiveActive`. All other variants reduce opacity to `0.7` on press.

## Accessibility

The inlined `useButton` hook (sourced from `@ddsrn/headless/button`) handles:

- `accessibilityRole="button"` on the `Pressable`
- `accessibilityState={{ disabled }}` — announced by screen readers
- Auto-derived `accessibilityLabel` from string `children`
- Dev warning when icon-only button is missing `accessibilityLabel`
- Dev warning when `variant="link"` has no icon

## Token usage

All colour and spacing values are derived from the active theme via `useTheme()`:

| Style property | Token |
|---------------|-------|
| Background (primary) | `theme.interaction.colorInteractiveDefault` |
| Background (active) | `theme.interaction.colorInteractiveActive` |
| Text/border (secondary) | `theme.interaction.colorInteractiveDefault` |
| Text (primary) | `theme.interaction.colorInteractiveInverse` |
| Border radius | `theme.borderRadius.pill` |
| Padding horizontal (md) | 16px |
| Padding horizontal (sm) | 12px |
| Min height (md) | 36px |
| Min height (sm) | 28px |
| Font size | `theme.typographyTokens.size16` |
| Font weight | `theme.typographyTokens.weight.bold` |

## Examples

### All variants

```tsx
import { Button } from './design-system/Button';
import { View } from 'react-native';
import { tokens } from './design-system/theme/tokens';

function ButtonDemo() {
  return (
    <View style={{ gap: tokens.spacing.sm }}>
      <Button variant="primary" onPress={() => {}}>Primary</Button>
      <Button variant="secondary" onPress={() => {}}>Secondary</Button>
      <Button variant="tertiary" onPress={() => {}}>Tertiary</Button>
      <Button variant="link" onPress={() => {}}>Link</Button>
    </View>
  );
}
```

### Disabled state

```tsx
<Button disabled onPress={() => {}}>
  Unavailable
</Button>
```

### Full width

```tsx
<Button isFullWidth onPress={() => {}}>
  Confirm order
</Button>
```

### Small size

```tsx
<Button size="sm" variant="secondary" onPress={() => {}}>
  Dismiss
</Button>
```

### Icon with label

```tsx
<Button leftIcon={<MyIcon />} onPress={() => {}}>
  Add to basket
</Button>
```

### Icon-only (requires accessibilityLabel)

```tsx
<Button
  leftIcon={<CloseIcon />}
  accessibilityLabel="Close dialog"
  onPress={() => {}}
/>
```

Note

See Button for usage guidance, accessibility advice, and platform behaviour.

The main screen of rn-expo-migration-showcase. Demonstrates TopBar, Heading, BodyText, and Button from the standalone design system.

`src/ComponentShowcase.tsx` is the single screen that drives the entire showcase. It uses all five standalone design-system components and runs unchanged on iOS, Android, and Expo Web.

## What is on screen

```
┌─────────────────────────────┐
│  Component Showcase  (TopBar)│
├─────────────────────────────┤
│                             │
│  DDS Standalone Components  │  ← Heading level 1
│                             │
│  These components are built │  ← BodyText md
│  from React Native          │
│  primitives...              │
│                             │
│  Interactive Button         │  ← Heading level 2, visualSize headline4
│                             │
│  Tap the button below...    │  ← BodyText md (live state)
│                             │
│  [ Tap me ]                 │  ← Button primary
│                             │
│  Migration phases           │  ← Heading level 2
│  Phase 1 - ...              │  ← BodyText sm × 5
│  Phase 2 - ...              │
│  ...                        │
└─────────────────────────────┘
```

## Source

```tsx
// src/ComponentShowcase.tsx

import { Heading }  from './design-system/Heading';
import { BodyText } from './design-system/BodyText';
import { Button }   from './design-system/Button';
import { TopBar }   from './design-system/TopBar';
import { tokens }   from './design-system/theme/tokens';

export function ComponentShowcase() {
  const [tapCount, setTapCount] = useState(0);

  return (
    <SafeAreaView>
      <TopBar title="Component Showcase" />
      <ScrollView>
        <Heading headingLevel="1">DDS Standalone Components</Heading>
        <BodyText size="md">...</BodyText>

        <Heading headingLevel="2" visualSize="headline4">Interactive Button</Heading>
        <BodyText size="md">{tapLabel}</BodyText>
        <Button onPress={() => setTapCount(c => c + 1)}>Tap me</Button>

        <Heading headingLevel="2" visualSize="headline4">Migration phases</Heading>
        <BodyText size="sm">Phase 1 - Standalone bare React Native</BodyText>
        <BodyText size="sm">Phase 2 - Expo SDK</BodyText>
        <BodyText size="sm">Phase 3 - Expo Web</BodyText>
        <BodyText size="sm">Phase 4 - Screenshot capture</BodyText>
        <BodyText size="sm">Phase 5 - Astro docs site</BodyText>
      </ScrollView>
    </SafeAreaView>
  );
}
```

## Key facts

- **Never modified** across any phase of the migration
- **Identical output** on iOS, Android, and Expo Web
- **No external imports** beyond `react-native` and `react-native-safe-area-context`
- **5 tests** verifying render, content, and button interaction (`__tests__/ComponentShowcase.test.tsx`)
